text:
I'm 61, so I read slowly and kept asking one thing: **what's left in my pocket at the end?** Here's how it went.

One thing first. A small dark box headed **"מס רק במכירה"** ("tax only when you sell") stayed open on the left of every screen, from top to bottom. It covered part of the page each time. Some numbers on the left were hidden from me, including the yearly-return box at the top and part of the currency-hedging tables.

## 1. What I would do, and how sure I am

I'd open an account at **Psagot (פסגות טרייד)**. Each month I'd buy **"ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)"**, fund number 5139282. That's the top line, marked **"הבחירה שלכם · ★ הזול"** ("your choice · the cheapest").

What it means for my money, using the page's example (10,000 ₪ now, 500 ₪ a month, 10 years):
- I put in **70,000 ₪**.
- I end with about **86,492 ₪**, in today's money, after fees and tax.
- The account fees come to **1,057 ₪** over 10 years, under 9 ₪ a month.
- The fund's fee is almost nothing: **"דמי ניהול: 0% קבועים 0% משתנים 0.02% נאמן"** (0% fixed, 0% variable, 0.02% trustee fee).

**How sure am I? About 70% on the account, less on the fund.**
- **The account:** I'm fairly sure about Psagot. My own bank, Leumi, comes out at **83,396 ₪**, about 3,000 ₪ less. That's real money. Some brokers lose me more than 20,000 ₪ (**"מיטב טרייד 63,507"**).
- **The fund:** the runner-up, Altshuler Shacham, is only **"43- ₪"** worse over ten years. That's nothing, so I'd be happy with either. What worries me about Ylin Lapidot is **"שנה אחת"** (one year): it has only one year of history. Altshuler's figure is also for one year, while the next ones have four. A 0% fee that new could be a launch offer, and I couldn't find out whether it can go up.
- **Currency hedging:** I would not take the hedged fund (**"מנוטרלת מט"ח"**). The page says hedging costs **"2.1 עד 3.3 נקודות בשנה"** (2.1 to 3.3 percentage points a year). Its result is **"בין +2,212 ל־ 23,766-"**, a range far too wide for me.

## 2. Parts I actually used

- The top: **"איפה ואיך הכי זול להשקיע במדד, לאורך זמן"** ("where and how to invest in an index most cheaply, for the long term"), the index buttons (I pressed S&P 500), and my amounts.
- The result box: **"הפקדתם 70,000"** (you deposited 70,000) next to **"86,492"**, and the runner-up at **"86,449"**.
- **"עלות אצלכם, לעומת הזוג השני"** (your cost compared with the runner-up): "החשבון 1 ₪ יותר, הקרן 58 ₪ פחות, המס 14 ₪ יותר" (the account costs 1 ₪ more, the fund 58 ₪ less, tax 14 ₪ more).
- The right-hand list, **"כל החשבונות"** (all accounts), ranked by what's left.
- The left-hand list, **"כל הקרנות על מדד S&P 500"** (all S&P 500 funds), mainly the shekel figures on the far left.
- **"מתחילים מבחירה אחת, ורואים מה משפר אותה ובכמה"** ("start from one choice and see what improves it, and by how much"), with the two tables "חשבון אחר, אותה קרן" (another account, same fund) and "סוג קרן אחר, אותו חשבון" (another fund type, same account).

## 3. Block by block

| Block | What I did | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Menu and index buttons | Used | Simple: I picked S&P 500. |
| S&P 500 description | Read | Clear. "**מושקע בדולרים**" (invested in dollars) told me the dollar matters. |
| Inputs (amount today, monthly, years, %) | Used | The % box was hidden under the popup. I only learned it was 7% from a table much further down. |
| "אינפלציה" button and the exchange-rate line | Skimmed | I understood "בכסף של היום" (in today's money). I didn't dare press the button. |
| Result: 70,000 → 86,492 | **Used most** | This is exactly my question. |
| Cost breakdown bar | Skimmed | Too many colours. The three words below it, "החשבון / הקרן / המס" (account / fund / tax), were enough. |
| Account list (right) | Used | Clear: name, amount left, and the cost under it. |
| Fund list (left) | Partly used, partly confused | The shekel figures helped. The coloured tags confused me (details below). |
| Psagot pricing note | Confused | "**קנייה חודשית מחושבת כהוראת קבע: 3 מתוך 15 הבנקים...**" (a monthly purchase is counted as a standing order: 3 of the 15 banks...). I read it twice and still didn't fully follow. |
| "לא בחישוב" (not in the calculation) notes under banks | Skimmed | They're discounts for young people, soldiers and students. None of them is me. |
| Foreign funds (iShares, Vanguard) | Skipped after one look | "**אין מחיר כאן**" (no price here), "**עיזבון אמריקאי**" (American estate tax), "**צריך טופס W-8BEN**" (needs a W-8BEN form). Not for me. |
| "מה כתוב בפרסום, מול התעריפון" (what the adverts say vs. the price list) | Skimmed | It was good to learn that adverts can mislead. I didn't open the individual claims. |
| "מה הכי משנה את מה שיישאר לכם" (what changes your result most) | Used the table, ignored the chart | The lesson was "**השנים**" (the years): two more years adds 19,116 ₪. At 61 that hits home. |
| "עם נטרול מט"ח או בלי" (with or without currency hedging) | Read the top boxes, skimmed the rest | The box with "2.1 עד 3.3" persuaded me. The year-by-year table was too much, and partly hidden. |
| "השורה התחתונה" (the bottom line) | Read | It confirmed there's no clear answer on hedging. |
| Step chart (79,176 → 86,492) | Used | It finally showed me that the account matters more than the fund: +4,972 from the account, +2,344 from the fund. |
| The two tables under it | Used the right-hand one | That's where I saw Leumi and Hapoalim against Psagot. |
| Footnotes at the bottom | Read | "**האתר לא ממליץ על מדד**" (the site doesn't recommend an index) and "**נתונים נכון ל־05.11.2026**" (data as of 05.11.2026). Good to know. |

## 4. In the lists, tables and charts

**What I looked at:**
- The account list: the bank name, the large number (what's left), and the small number under it (cost).
- The fund list: the red number on the far left, e.g. **"−447 ₪"** and **"−4,492 ₪"**, which is how much less than the cheapest I'd end with. The fund name, too.
- **"שנה אחת" vs "4 שנים"** (one year vs four years) under the percentages.
- The tables near the end: **"נשאר בסוף"** (left at the end) and **"לעומת עכשיו"** (compared with now). Green "עוד" means more money and red "פחות" means less. That was clear.
- The "what matters most" table: the **"ההפרש"** column (the difference).

**What I ignored:**
- The colours in the cost bar (orange, red, yellow, green, purple).
- The coloured line chart of the four factors.
- The bar chart of the dollar since 2002.
- Most tags, such as "צוברת" (accumulating) and "חשיפה לדולר" (dollar exposure).
- The **"+0.37%"** figures. I didn't know whether that means a return or something else.

## 5. What I didn't understand

- **"4D" and "4A"**: what do they mean?
- **"קרן מחקה" vs "קרן סל"** (tracker fund vs ETF): what's the difference for me? Why are ETFs generally more expensive here?
- **"+0.37% בשנה · שנה אחת"**: plus relative to what? There's an explanation, **"מול המדד: כמה הקרן הקדימה (+) או פיגרה (−)"** ("against the index: how far the fund got ahead (+) or fell behind (−)"), but it sat at the bottom, half under the popup.
- **"מס גם על שינוי המטבע"** ("tax on the currency change too"): will I pay tax on a profit that only came from the dollar?
- **"עמלות זו על זו"** (fees on fees) in the colour legend.
- The popup's text: "**...זו שאלה פתוחה, ולכן הדרך מוצגת בלי דירוג**" ("it's an open question, so this route is shown without a ranking"). I understood it relates to foreign funds, but why was it open over everything the whole time?
- **"עוד לא נאסף"** (not collected yet): not collected by whom?

## 6. What I wanted to know and couldn't find

- **Can Ylin Lapidot's 0% fee go up?** Is it a temporary offer? That's the biggest question for me.
- **How exactly is tax calculated at the end?** Is it 25% only on the profit? Is there anything for my age?
- **What if I need the money in 5 years** rather than 10? I could have changed the years myself, but I would have liked a ready answer.
- **How safe is the money** if Psagot or the fund manager gets into trouble?
- **How to start:** opening an account, setting up a standing order, and whether a standing order is even possible for this fund.
- **What's the difference between 86,492 and 86,449** apart from the 43 ₪? Is one fund larger, older, or more stable?

## 7. If half the page had to go

First to go:
1. The foreign funds (iShares, Vanguard, IVV, VOO). They have no price and need forms.
2. The year-by-year hedging tables and the dollar chart since 2002. The one box saying "hedging costs 2.1–3.3% a year" is enough.
3. The coloured line chart under "what matters most". Keep the table.
4. The list of advert claims for each broker.
5. The colourful cost bar.
6. The "not in the calculation" discounts for young people and soldiers. They aren't me.

I would keep the top with my amounts and the result, the account list, the left-hand fund list with the shekel figures, and the step chart. Those four parts told me what to do with my money.
